messages:
anya: FYI discovered a regression after the RBAC roles->role-mappings refactor — a staging tenant could enumerate another org's projects. Repro steps below.

anya: repro: use service-mapping endpoint with bound service-account id from tenant A, call GET /v1/projects?org=tenant-B and it returned list.

devin: omg, do you have a curl/log snippet?

anya: snippet: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sa:staging-abc' 
  'https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/projects?org=org-b'```

anya: response body had 200 + list of projects from org-b. looks like the service-account lookup fell back to a global mapping during the new merge logic.

maria: that matches the role-merge codepath I touched. I added a fallback to legacy bindings when project-level bindings are empty — maybe the fallback used org-wide index incorrectly.

kevin: can someone grep for where we resolve "bound_org_id" vs "resolved_org" in authorization service? I'm worried it's using the request org param rather than asserting SA's owning org.

devin: grep result: authz/resolve.go line 228 does `if mapping == nil { mapping = globalIndex.Lookup(sa)` } — that looks suspicious. sending a quick patch.

maria: if that's true, rollback the fallback and add a defensive assertion: `assert(mapping.OrgID == sa.OrgID)` before allowing list.

kevin: +1. Also audit: we need to find who accessed cross-org resources. @audit-bot can you pull last 24h authz checks for that SA id `sa:staging-abc`?

audit-bot: query started: "SELECT ts, caller_sa, target_org, action FROM authz_logs WHERE caller_sa='sa:staging-abc' AND ts > now()-24h". Results: 5 hits. Returning masked log lines.

anya: logs show the GETs happened only in staging env. no production SA spotted so far, but let's treat as P0 until confirmed.

maria: pushing hotfix PR removing global fallback and adding explicit org bind check. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/authz/pulls/4827 — includes unit tests + integration test that simulates cross-org request.

devin: rolling out patch to staging now. deploying to canary cluster first.

kevin: mitigation steps: 1) revoke the staging SA token, 2) rotate any bindings created in the window, 3) run full audit for last 7 days.

anya: revoked token and noted for customer-facing comms if it affects external testers.

maria: opened postmortem stub in /docs/incidents/priv-esc-staging-1749990001.md and scheduled 30m follow-up. Will include root cause, fix, and tests to prevent reintroduction.

devin: after canary looks good I'll promote to all staging clusters. I'll also add a linting rule in CI to forbid globalIndex fallback without org check.

kevin: one more: double-check KMS key access checks — if the SA could list projects, could it also request decrypt on cross-org keys? we need to verify KMS bindings are separate.

maria: checked KMS logs quickly — no cross-org decrypt attempts observed. KMS binding uses a separate check that queries project-level key bindings, unaffected by this merge bug.

anya: ok good. next: draft customer note for staging testers explaining cause and steps, but not a broad security disclosure since no prod impact. :thumbsup:

audit-bot: audit query completed: 7-day scan shows no other SA with same pattern. Marking incident severity: staging-only, escalate if new hits appear.

kevin: thanks team — follow-up in 30m postmortem. Keep thread updated with rollout status.
